The three nodes form a single conceptual cluster: the spiritual inheritance of the righteous, described from three angles (structural: 310 worlds; eschatological: World to Come; experiential: pleasures and delights). concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The king (מלך) is used in the teaching as an example and paradigm (line 8: the king's greatness is in his heart-knowledge), not as a concept being given a bechina equation of its own. The teaching uses the king as a mashal (illustrative analogy) to establish that 'greatness = heart-knowledge.' The מלך is not identified as a bechina-equivalent of another concept — the king is the vehicle through which 'לב מלכים' is explained. Excluded from bechina packages; the king is a narrative example, not a bechina-node. The node 'לב מלכים' (the king's heart) is included as a bechina-concept because it is the actual concept being equated with the heart's infinite nature; 'מלך' as a person-category is not.

The tzaddik appears in line 9 as the person who has all the pleasures and worlds in his heart ('הַצַּדִּיק בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹ'). He is the actualized case — the person whose heart is full — but the teaching does not establish a bechina equation 'the tzaddik IS the heart's fullness' or 'the tzaddik = the 310 worlds.' He is an eitza-node: the heart's fullness (Package 1) + having all the worlds (Package 2) → the tzaddik is the one who achieves this. The contrast with the neighbor (who feels nothing) is eitza/narrative, not bechina. Excluded from bechina packages.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: גדולות הבורא / גדולת הבורא (the greatness of the Creator)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The Creator's greatness appears in lines 4 and 7 as the object of contemplation — the destination of the kal va-chomer reasoning. Line 4: 'רְאֵה וְהָבֵן וַחֲכַם גְּדֻלַּת הַבּוֹרֵא' — see and understand the Creator's greatness. This is an eitza-destination: the heart's infinite capacity (Package 1) → one can reason upward → to grasp the Creator's greatness. The Creator's greatness is not declared bechina-equivalent to the heart; it is what the heart's infinity enables you to estimate through kal va-chomer. Excluded from bechina packages.

Divine Providence appears in line 5 as a scale: 'אֵינוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל חֵלֶק אֶחָד מֵאַלְפֵי אֲלָפִים מֵהַשְׁגָּחַת הַבּוֹרֵא' — the Divinity in the heart is 'not even one part in thousands of thousands of the Creator's Providence.' This is a quantitative framing of scale, not a bechina equation. Providence is used to demonstrate the relative size of the Divinity in the heart, not to establish that Providence and the heart share the same essential nature. Excluded from bechina packages.

Dominion (ממשלה) appears in line 8 alongside the king's greatness and pleasure as all being located in the heart ('עִקַּר גְּדֻלּוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ וְתַעֲנוּגוֹ וּמֶמְשַׁלְתּוֹ הוּא רַק בַּלֵּב'). One could argue that ממשלה is a bechina-equivalent of לב in this teaching. However, the text presents it as a quality that resides in the heart rather than as something the heart IS. The heart's greatness, pleasure, and dominion are 'in the heart' (eitza: the heart contains/produces these qualities). This is slightly different from the primary bechina claims where the heart IS the content (Divinity, infinity). Excluded as a secondary attribution rather than a primary bechina identity.

Gan Eden appears in line 1 as the setting of the opening scenario — the place where two people sit next to each other, one experiencing all pleasures, the other feeling nothing. It is structurally parallel to עולם הבא (which closes the teaching in line 10) and could be considered bechina-equivalent. However, the teaching does not explicitly equate them through a formula; Gan Eden is the opening frame (scenario) and עולם הבא is the closing conclusion (identity statement). A weak bechina proposed as a secondary edge in the additions for עולם הבא; not treated as a primary standalone addition.

Wisdom and intellect do not appear in Torah #191. The teaching is cited as cross-referencing Torah #49 ('כַּמְבֹאָר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר — לעיל בסימן מט') for the teaching about Divinity being in the heart, but Torah #49's concepts (sekhel, chokhmah) are not developed in Torah #191 itself. Excluded from Torah #191 packages — they belong to Torah #49's packages.

The heavens and earth appear in lines 2-3 as a scale of comparison: 'שָׁמַיִם לָרוּם וָאָרֶץ לָעֹמֶק' (heaven is for height and earth for depth). They are used to show that the heart exceeds even the infinite heavens and earth in its capacity — a kal va-chomer comparison tool. They are not equated with the heart through a bechina formula; they are the scale being exceeded. The Talmudic saying about the oceans and pens is also a scale-illustration. Excluded from bechina packages.

analysis_notes.note_on_bechina_language: Torah #191 uses three types of bechina language: (1) the explicit word 'בְּחִינוֹת' (aspects/dimensions) in line 5 — 'שֶׁנִּמְצָא שָׁם רַק בְּחִינוֹת אֱלֹקוּת' — this is the core bechina vocabulary; (2) essence statements using 'עִקַּר... הוּא' ('the essential... is') — a Rebbe Nachman formula equivalent to 'is a bechina of': 'עִקַּר הָאֱלֹקוּת הוּא בְּהַלֵּב' and 'עִקַּר הַרְגָּשַׁת תַּעֲנוּג... הַכֹּל הוּא בַּלֵּב'; (3) identity through co-listing — pairing תענוגים ושעשועים with שי"ט עולמות and עולם הבא as a single unit in four separate statements, establishing they refer to the same reality. The repeated use of 'לב מלכים אין חקר' (three times) as the central identity-formula for the heart is also a bechina pattern — the verse is not proof of an external claim but IS the bechina statement about the heart's essential nature.
analysis_notes.note_on_teaching_structure: Torah #191 is a ten-sentence philosophical meditation with a clear frame structure: it opens (line 1) and closes (lines 9-10) with the same paradox — two people in Gan Eden, one with all pleasures, the other with nothing. The middle develops the paradox's solution through a kal va-chomer argument (lines 2-8). The two packages capture the two poles of the teaching: Package 1 (לב and אלקות) is the mechanism (why the heart can contain infinitely); Package 2 (עולם הבא / 310 worlds / pleasures) is the content (what the full heart contains). The cross-package eitza is: heart-contains-Divinity (Pkg 1) → heart-can-contain-310-worlds (Pkg 2).
